item.title: Shakira Thrills Crowd of 2 Million With Free Concert on Brazil’s Copacabana Beach
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: "Welcome to our podcast, where we bring you the latest in music and entertainment. Tonight, we're talking about a record-breaking concert that took place on one of the world's most iconic beaches. Shakira recently performed a free concert on Copacabana Beach in Rio de Janeiro, and it was a night to remember.
[Short music clip: Shakira's "Hips Don't Lie"]
Host: "The concert, which was part of her Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran world tour, drew an estimated 2 million people to the beach. That's right, 2 million fans came out to see the Colombian superstar perform her hits. The show kicked off around 11 pm, with skywriting drones flying overhead, spelling out 'I love you Brazil' in Portuguese.
[Short music clip: Shakira's "La Tortura"]
Host: "Shakira took the stage, speaking fondly of her first visit to Brazil over three decades ago. She performed fan favorites like 'Hips Don't Lie', 'La Tortura', and 'La Bicicleta'. She also celebrated women's resilience, saying 'Us women, every time we fall, we get up a little wiser'.
[Short music clip: Shakira's "BZRP Music Sessions #53/66"]
Host: "The concert was a huge success, with Rio Mayor Eduardo Cavaliere saying it made history in the city. Fans like 38-year-old accountant Erica Monteiro praised Shakira for representing the strength of the Latino community.
[Short music clip: Shakira's "Waka Waka"]
Host: "The concert was also seen as a celebration of Latin American identity, with fans like Hellem Souza da Silva saying it helped consolidate Brazil's connection to the region. And with fans starting to arrive on the beach as early as Saturday morning, it was clear that this was going to be a special night.
[Outro music plays]
Host: "That's all for tonight's podcast. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll see you next time!"
